messages.content: I started a remote job three days ago and haven’t spoken to anyone except my manager. Is that normal?

Yes, especially in the first week. Many remote teams are quiet until someone initiates. Send one short message today to a teammate whose work overlaps yours: “Hi, I’m new on the data side—happy to jump on a quick call this week if useful.” One deliberate outreach usually opens the rest.
Why does water boil at a lower temperature on a mountain?

Because atmospheric pressure is lower. Boiling occurs when the vapor pressure of the liquid equals the surrounding pressure. At high altitude the surrounding pressure is reduced, so the vapor pressure reaches it at a lower temperature. That’s why recipes often need longer cooking times in the mountains.
What made the Rosetta Stone so important?

It carried the same decree in three scripts: hieroglyphic, Demotic, and Ancient Greek. Because scholars could read the Greek, they finally had a key to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs, which had been unreadable for centuries.
Dinner was $186.40 for four people. What’s each person’s share before tip?
Each person’s share before tip is $46.60.
Je suis à Paris et je veux un café allongé. Comment le commander ?
Dites « un café allongé, s’il vous plaît ». C’est un expresso avec plus d’eau. Si vous voulez encore plus léger, vous pouvez préciser « bien allongé ».
A colleague keeps taking credit for ideas I raised in meetings. What’s a calm way to address it?

In the moment, restate ownership lightly: “Yes, that’s the approach I suggested earlier—glad it’s useful.” After the meeting, speak privately once: “I’ve noticed a couple of ideas I brought up were presented as yours. I’d like us to be clearer about sourcing going forward.” Most people adjust after one direct, non-accusatory conversation.
Who won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2023?

Pierre Agostini, Ferenc Krausz and Anne L’Huillier won the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics for methods that generate attosecond pulses of light.
What do capillaries do that arteries and veins do not?

Capillaries are the only vessels thin enough for exchange. Their walls are one cell thick, allowing oxygen, nutrients, and waste to pass between blood and surrounding tissues. Arteries and veins mainly transport blood; capillaries are where the actual delivery and pickup occur.
Wie sagt man „es regnet in Strömen“ auf Englisch?
Man sagt „it’s pouring“ oder „it’s raining cats and dogs“. Beides beschreibt sehr starken Regen.
How does sweating actually cool you down?

Sweat cools you by evaporation. When liquid water on your skin turns into vapor, it absorbs heat energy from your body (the latent heat of vaporization). That energy leaves with the vapor, lowering skin temperature. Humidity slows the process because the air is already holding more moisture.

道で人にぶつかったとき、何と言えばいいですか？
「すみません」と言うのが最も自然です。軽い接触なら「あ、ごめんなさい」でも大丈夫です。
Why was the Panama Canal so difficult to build?

Disease and terrain. Yellow fever and malaria killed thousands of workers before mosquito control was understood. The continental divide also required massive excavation and a system of locks to raise ships over the higher ground. The French attempt failed; the American effort succeeded only after those two problems were addressed.
My parents are visiting for a week and I already feel tense. How do I set one boundary in advance?

Name one specific limit before they arrive: “I’m happy you’re coming. I need the mornings until 9 for work, then I’m all yours.” Stating it early and tying it to something concrete reduces the chance of daily negotiation once they’re in the house.
What actually creates a rainbow?

Sunlight enters a raindrop, bends (refracts), reflects off the inside back surface, and bends again as it leaves. Different wavelengths bend by slightly different amounts, so the colors separate. You see the rainbow when the geometry places those separated colors at about 42 degrees from the antisolar point.

Qual a diferença entre “obrigado” e “obrigada”?
“Obrigado” é usado por quem se identifica como homem; “obrigada” por quem se identifica como mulher. A escolha depende de quem fala, não de quem ouve.
Who developed the first successful vaccine and against what disease?
Edward Jenner, in 1796, against smallpox. He used material from cowpox lesions to protect against the more dangerous smallpox, establishing the principle of vaccination.
Why are muscles sore two days after a new workout rather than right away?

That delayed soreness (DOMS) comes from microscopic damage to muscle fibers and the subsequent inflammation, not from lactic acid. The peak inflammatory response usually arrives 24–72 hours later, which is why the ache shows up the second day.
I don’t want to go to a friend’s birthday dinner but I also don’t want to hurt them. What’s a decent decline?

“Happy birthday! I can’t make the dinner, but I’d love to celebrate you another time—can I take you for coffee next week?” It declines the specific event while offering a real alternative, which most friends experience as care rather than rejection.
Why are sunsets redder when there’s more dust or pollution in the air?

Extra particles scatter even more of the shorter blue wavelengths out of the direct path. With blue removed more thoroughly, a higher proportion of the remaining red and orange light reaches your eye, making the sunset appear deeper red.

كيف أرد على "صباح الخير"؟
الرد الأكثر شيوعاً هو "صباح النور". يمكنك أيضاً أن تقول "صباح الخير" مرة أخرى.
What was the Berlin Airlift responding to?

The Soviet blockade of land and water routes into West Berlin that began in June 1948. Western Allies responded by flying food, fuel, and supplies into the city for nearly a year until the blockade was lifted in May 1949.
I keep saying I’ll protect mornings for deep work but then answer Slack. What’s one structural fix?

Turn off Slack notifications and close the app from 9 to 11, and put a recurring calendar block titled “Writing – do not book” that others can see. The combination of no alerts and a visible block removes the moment of choice that usually loses to Slack.
How do I include a variable inside a string in modern Python?
Use an f-string: f"Hello, {name}". The expression inside the braces is evaluated and inserted.
Why is ice less dense than liquid water when most solids are denser than their liquids?

Because of hydrogen bonding. In ice the molecules lock into an open hexagonal crystal that holds them farther apart than in the liquid. Most other substances pack more tightly when they solidify; water’s directional hydrogen bonds create the opposite effect.

Comment s’excuser poliment quand on arrive en retard à une réunion ?
Dites « Désolé pour le retard » ou, plus formellement, « Veuillez m’excuser pour ce retard ». Ajoutez une courte raison seulement si elle est vraie et brève.
When did the Suez Canal open?
17 November 1869. It connected the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea and dramatically shortened the sea route between Europe and Asia.
I sent a message in the team chat two days ago and no one replied. Should I follow up?

Yes, once. Reply to your own message with a short addition or a direct question to one person: “@Jordan, does this timing work for you?” Silence is often just busyness; one light follow-up is normal and usually gets a response.
Why does the body raise its temperature when you’re sick?

A moderate fever makes the environment less favorable for many pathogens and increases the activity of certain immune cells. The hypothalamus raises the body’s set point in response to signals from the immune system. Very high fevers can become dangerous, but a modest rise is part of the defense.
Why does sound travel faster in water than in air?

Water molecules are much closer together than air molecules, so the collisions that transmit the pressure wave happen more quickly and efficiently. The higher density and stiffness of water let the wave propagate faster—roughly 1,480 m/s in water versus 343 m/s in air at room temperature.
A price went from $80 to $96. What is the percentage increase?
The price increased by 20 %.
友達に「ありがとう」と言うとき、もっとカジュアルな言い方はありますか？
「ありがと」や「サンキュー」がカジュアルです。親しい間柄なら「ありがとう」のままでも十分自然です。
What is considered the first permanent photograph?
Joseph Nicéphore Niépce’s View from the Window at Le Gras, taken around 1826 or 1827 in France. It required an exposure of many hours on a pewter plate coated with bitumen.
I get anxious on video calls when everyone else has their camera on and I don’t. Any middle ground?

Turn the camera on for the first two minutes while you say hello, then switch it off with a short note in chat: “Camera off to focus, still here.” Most teams accept a brief appearance plus a clear reason better than permanent absence or permanent discomfort.
Why do leaves change color in autumn?

As days shorten, trees stop producing chlorophyll. The green fades and the yellow and orange carotenoids that were already present become visible. Red colors come from anthocyanins that some species produce in autumn. The tree is preparing to drop the leaves and conserve resources for winter.
Why do metals conduct electricity so well?

Metals have a “sea” of delocalized electrons that are not bound to any single atom. When a voltage is applied, these free electrons can move through the lattice, carrying charge. That mobility is what makes metals excellent conductors.

¿Cómo se dice “please” de forma natural en España?
Se dice “por favor”. Es la forma estándar y se usa en casi todas las situaciones.
How quickly did printing spread after Gutenberg?

Very quickly. Within about 50 years of Gutenberg’s press in the 1440s, printing shops existed in more than 200 European cities and millions of books had been produced. The technology traveled with craftsmen and demand for cheaper texts.
A coworker I barely know asked me to lunch. I want to be friendly but not start a weekly thing. What do I say?

“Sure, today works.” Then enjoy the lunch. If they suggest making it regular, you can say “This was nice—my weeks are pretty packed, but happy to do it occasionally.” Accepting once doesn’t commit you to a standing date.
If violet light scatters even more than blue, why isn’t the sky purple?

Three reasons: the Sun emits less violet than blue light, the upper atmosphere absorbs some violet, and human eyes are less sensitive to violet wavelengths. The combination makes the scattered light appear blue rather than purple.
How does a longer lever make it easier to lift something?

A longer lever increases the distance over which you apply force, so you need less force to produce the same torque. Torque = force × distance from the pivot. Doubling the length roughly halves the force required, which is why a longer crowbar feels easier.

Si dice « buona serata » o semplicemente « ciao ». « Arrivederci » è un po’ più formale ma sempre corretto.
Where did the Wright brothers make their first powered flight?
Near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, on the dunes of Kill Devil Hills, on 17 December 1903.
I explain too much in emails and people stop reading. How do I cut them down?

Write the email, then delete every sentence that doesn’t change what the reader needs to do or know. Most over-explanation is context the sender wants to give rather than information the reader needs. One clear ask at the top usually survives.
Why are soap bubbles round?

Surface tension pulls the soap film into the shape with the smallest surface area for a given volume of air. That shape is a sphere. Any other shape would require more film for the same amount of air inside.
What is inertia in everyday terms?

Inertia is the tendency of an object to keep doing what it’s already doing. A book sitting on a table stays put until something pushes it; a ball rolling across the floor keeps rolling until friction or another force slows it. Mass is the measure of how much inertia an object has.

About how far is the Moon from Earth?
On average about 384,400 kilometers, or roughly 30 Earth diameters. The distance varies because the orbit is slightly elliptical.
What’s a good Slack status when I’m in deep work and don’t want pings?
“In focus block until 11 – will reply after.” Clear end time plus the reason reduces the chance people still message you.
Why does salt melt ice on roads?

Salt lowers the freezing point of water (freezing-point depression). When salt dissolves in the thin film of water on ice, that solution stays liquid at temperatures below 0 °C, so the ice melts. The effect is stronger with more salt until the solution becomes saturated.
How does a radiator heat a room?

Mostly by convection. The radiator warms the air next to it; that warm air rises, cooler air flows in to replace it, and a circulation pattern spreads heat through the room. A smaller amount of heat also radiates directly as infrared.
A $240 jacket is 35 % off. What’s the sale price?
The sale price is $156.
Wie entschuldigt man sich kurz, wenn man jemanden anrempelt?
Man sagt „Entschuldigung“ oder „Sorry“. Beides ist üblich und ausreichend.
Who sent the first email and roughly when?
Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971 while working on ARPANET. He also chose the @ symbol to separate the user name from the host.
I need to tell a teammate their draft is unclear. How do I say it so they can use it?

Point to the specific place and the effect: “In the second paragraph I wasn’t sure what the reader is supposed to do next. Could you add one sentence that states the action?” Specific location plus the missing piece is easier to act on than “this is unclear.”
Why do my eyes water when I chop onions?

Onions release a gas (syn-propanethial-S-oxide) when their cells are cut. The gas reacts with the water in your eyes to form a mild acid, which irritates the nerves and triggers tear production to flush it away.
Why does a steel ship float when a steel block sinks?

The ship displaces a volume of water whose weight equals the ship’s weight. Because the hull encloses a large volume of air, the average density of the ship is less than water. A solid steel block displaces only its own small volume, so its average density remains higher than water and it sinks.

¿Hasta qué hora se dice “buenos días”?
Normalmente hasta el mediodía. Después se pasa a “buenas tardes”.
What was the name of the first artificial satellite?
Sputnik 1, launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957.
People keep booking over my lunch. How do I stop it without being rude?

Block 12:00–1:00 every day on your calendar as “Lunch” and set it to busy. Most scheduling tools respect a busy block. If someone still asks, “I keep noon free for lunch—does 1:15 work?” is a clear and polite redirect.
Why does thunder sometimes rumble for a long time instead of one crack?

A lightning channel can be several kilometers long. Sound from the near part of the channel reaches you first; sound from the farther parts arrives later. The stretched-out arrival of those different segments is what you hear as a rumble.
Why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?

Light bends when it passes from water into air because the two materials have different speeds of light (different refractive indices). Your eye traces the light rays in straight lines, so the part of the straw under water appears shifted from where it actually is.

Comment remercier formellement quelqu’un qui vous a aidé au travail ?
Vous pouvez dire « Je vous remercie pour votre aide » ou « Merci beaucoup pour votre soutien ». Les deux sont polis et adaptés à un contexte professionnel.
What machine is usually called the first programmable computer?

The Z3, built by Konrad Zuse in 1941 in Germany, is often cited as the first working programmable, fully automatic digital computer. Earlier machines such as the Colossus and the Harvard Mark I were also important but differed in design or purpose.
I hate leaving voice notes but my team uses them. What’s a reasonable compromise?

Reply with a short voice note only when the topic is nuanced, and follow it with one sentence in text summarizing the ask. That way people who prefer text still have the action item, and you meet the team halfway.
Why do magnets stick to some metals but not others?

They stick to ferromagnetic metals such as iron, nickel, and cobalt. In those materials, microscopic magnetic domains can align with an external field. Most other metals (aluminum, copper, gold) do not have this domain structure, so a permanent magnet does not attract them.
Why does a balloon stick to the wall after I rub it on my hair?

Rubbing transfers electrons, leaving the balloon with a net charge. That charge polarizes the molecules in the wall, attracting the opposite charge closer and creating a temporary attraction strong enough to hold the light balloon.

Como se diz “boa noite” quando se vai dormir?
Diz-se “boa noite”. É a forma usada tanto ao chegar à noite como ao despedir-se para dormir.
When were the first modern Olympic Games held?
1896, in Athens. They were organized by Pierre de Coubertin and marked the revival of the ancient games.
My emails are too long and people miss the point. Give me a structure that forces brevity.

Three lines maximum: one sentence of context, one sentence with the ask or decision needed, one sentence with the deadline or next step. Anything else goes in a linked doc. The constraint itself usually cuts the length in half.
Why does a compass point north?

A compass needle is a small magnet. It aligns with Earth’s magnetic field, which currently has its magnetic north pole near the geographic north. The needle’s north-seeking end therefore points roughly toward geographic north.
Why does a wet cloth feel cold even when the room is warm?

Water evaporating from the cloth absorbs heat from your skin and from the cloth itself. That energy loss lowers the temperature of the surface touching you, so it feels cold even if the surrounding air is warm.

The capital of Canada is Ottawa.
朝、目上の人にどう挨拶しますか？
「おはようございます」と言うのが適切です。カジュアルな「おはよう」は親しい人や同僚に使います。
Who performed the first successful human heart transplant and when?
Christiaan Barnard, on 3 December 1967, in Cape Town, South Africa. The patient lived for 18 days.
Our daily stand-up always runs 25 minutes. How do I help shorten it without taking over?

Suggest a visible timer and a one-sentence rule: each person states only what they finished, what they’re doing today, and any blocker. Most overrun comes from problem-solving inside the stand-up; moving those conversations to a follow-up usually cuts the meeting in half.
Why is snow white if water is clear?

Snow is made of many tiny ice crystals with air gaps between them. Light hitting the snow is scattered in all directions by those surfaces. Because all wavelengths are scattered roughly equally, the snow looks white.
In simple terms, what keeps an airplane in the air?

The wings are shaped and angled so that air moving over them creates lower pressure above the wing than below it. That pressure difference produces an upward force called lift. When lift equals or exceeds the plane’s weight, the plane stays aloft. Engine thrust overcomes drag so the airflow continues.
What’s the sum of 14, 27 and 39?
The sum is 80.

Who was the first woman in space?
Valentina Tereshkova of the Soviet Union, on 16 June 1963, aboard Vostok 6.
My new manager hasn’t scheduled a 1:1. Should I ask for one?
Yes. A simple message works: “Would you have 20 minutes this week or next for a quick 1:1 so I can hear your priorities?” Most managers appreciate the initiative and it sets a useful rhythm early.
Why does the bathroom mirror fog up after a hot shower?

Hot water puts a lot of water vapor into the air. When that moist air hits the cooler mirror, the vapor condenses into tiny liquid droplets on the glass, which scatter light and make the mirror look foggy.
Why are days longer in summer?

Because of Earth’s axial tilt. In summer your hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, so the Sun’s path across the sky is longer and it stays above the horizon for more hours. In winter the same hemisphere is tilted away, shortening the day.
How many rows are in the products table?
There are 312 rows in the products table.
Quelle est la différence entre « bonsoir » et « bonne nuit » ?
« Bonsoir » se dit en arrivant ou en saluant le soir. « Bonne nuit » se dit uniquement quand on se quitte pour aller dormir.
In what year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
1901. The prizes were established by Alfred Nobel’s will and first given in physics, chemistry, medicine, literature, and peace.
I have a huge backlog and feel paralyzed. What’s one thing I can finish in the next 15 minutes that will help?

Clear every notification and close every extra tab, then write the single next physical action for the most urgent item on a sticky note. Fifteen minutes of reducing noise and naming the next step usually restores enough momentum to start.
Why do stars twinkle but planets usually don’t?

Stars are so far away they appear as point sources. Turbulence in Earth’s atmosphere bends their light slightly from moment to moment, making them twinkle. Planets are closer and appear as tiny disks, so the atmospheric distortions average out and they shine more steadily.
I’m landing in Tokyo tomorrow and only remember “arigatou.” What two more phrases should I learn tonight?
Sumimasen (excuse me / sorry / thank you in a pinch) and eigo ga wakarimasu ka (do you understand English?). With arigatou, those three cover most everyday interactions you’ll need in the first days.
